risks.risk: Dependence on the mining and commodity capex cycle, with the business concentrated on bulk material handling and mineral processing
risks.note: The Company states its products and services predominantly cater to Bulk Material Handling and Mineral Processing activities and that 'the business prospects of the Company are closely tied to these activities/industries'. It describes its markets as sensitive to global macroeconomic and commodity-cycle risks, so a downturn in mining investment transmits directly to both the products and the services book.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption - the 2026 Middle East conflict
risks.note: Management says heightened geopolitical tensions have increased volatility in energy prices, shipping routes and financial markets, potentially affecting mining investment cycles and cost structures. It is already visible in results: consolidated profitability was impacted despite higher revenue, primarily on account of the ongoing geopolitical situation in the Middle East and the loss at the Saudi Arabian subsidiary. Notably, the Risks and Concerns section states the Company 'does not perceive any major technological, operational, financial or environmental risks in the near future except for geopolitical tensions and their impact on the global economy' - geopolitics is the one risk management concedes as live.

risks.risk: Overseas subsidiary exposure - currency, labour, regulation and country risk
risks.note: Subsidiaries in Australia, Brazil and Chile are stated to be exposed to fluctuating commodity prices, labour-market rigidities, regulatory changes and currency volatility which may impact profitability. The outlook section repeats that Australia, the Middle East and Latin America carry geopolitical uncertainty, currency fluctuation and differing regulatory environments that could impact profitability and contract execution.

The industry is described as witnessing intensifying competition from international OEMs, low-cost regional players and integrated automation providers, increasing pricing pressure and shortening product-life cycles.

risks.risk: Technology transition risk - continuous investment required, customer adoption may lag
risks.note: As mining and industrial clients accelerate digital adoption, the Company must continuously invest in new technologies, skilled manpower and advanced diagnostics to remain competitive. Management adds that while it is strengthening predictive-maintenance, remote-monitoring and digital-optimisation capability, customer adoption rates may be gradual, requiring sustained investment and posing risks related to technology integration and return on investment.

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety at customer sites
risks.note: Flagged as a Risk in the BRSR material-issues table with negative financial implication: on-site servicing at mining, bulk-handling and industrial sites involves exposure to fire, chemical, machinery and fall hazards, and any safety failure can result in worker injury, regulatory action and reputational damage. Mitigation is a structured OHS management system covering risk assessments, safety training, PPE, permit-to-work and safety audits.

risks.risk: Product quality, reliability and lifecycle stewardship
risks.note: BRSR material issue flagged as both Risk and Opportunity: conveyor belt failure at customer sites can cause unplanned downtime and safety incidents, and the long product lifecycle creates a stewardship responsibility. Mitigation cited is ISO certification, customer-complaint tracking, rubber reclaim initiatives and in-house R&D on biodegradation of finished rubber waste.

risks.risk: Environmental compliance and resource dependence - water and GHG emissions
risks.note: Two BRSR material issues with negative financial implications: manufacturing depends on groundwater, raising consumption and scarcity exposure in the regions where Thejo operates; and energy-intensive rubber and polyurethane processing generates significant GHG emissions with growing customer decarbonisation expectations adding transition risk. The MD&A adds that environmental norms on emissions, water usage and workplace safety are tightening in key markets, potentially increasing compliance and operating costs.

themes.title: Refractories & metallurgical consumables
themes.need: Refractory and metallurgical-consumable makers earn recurring per-tonne pricing tied to steel/cement OUTPUT volumes - an annuity-like wear-parts thesis, not the producers own realisation cycle. Q1FY27 turned the graphite-electrode leg on PRICE rather than demand: HEG's standalone EBITDA swung from -INR 126cr in Q4FY26 to +INR 211cr at a 29% margin on LOWER volumes, entirely realisation and mix, after GrafTech announced $600-1,200/t and Tokai $930/t electrode price increases. The timing is unusually favourable - HEG's own price rises only take effect from October because its book is committed through Sept/Oct, while needle-coke inflation (+$200-300/t on 10-15% of electrode cost) hits the P&L only Nov-Jan. RAIN adds the calcined-petroleum-coke anode consumable into aluminium smelters (Carbon EBITDA up INR 1.63B as CPC prices ran $50-100 above the West on China's supply crunch); SMLT the cored-wire leg into steel mills.
themes.driver: Steel/cement output-volume growth driving per-tonne consumables demand; HEG's October price increases landing against needle-coke inflation arriving only Nov-Jan - Q3 is the quarter the margin-maintenance promise is decided.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Thejo Engineering is a premium engineering solutions provider to the mining, mineral processing and bulk material handling industries, and is one of the few companies in the sub-continent offering manufacturing, marketing and servicing activities under one roof.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company designs, develops, manufactures and supplies rubber and polyurethane-based engineered products for belt cleaning, spillage control, flow enhancement, impact and abrasion protection and screening applications, alongside adhesives and industrial machinery. It pairs that products business with an on-site services business covering installation, operation and maintenance of conveyor belts and allied technical services, delivered through a national network of branch, technical-service and O&M site offices. Customers are core-sector industries - steel, mining, mineral processing, aggregates and sand, power, chemical and fertiliser, cement and ports - served in India and, through five overseas subsidiaries and distributors, in Australasia, the Middle East, South America, North America, Sub-Sahara and West Africa.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global mining investment is strengthening, supported by sustained demand for iron ore, coal and battery minerals essential to the energy transition, driving requirements for conveyor systems, wear-protection solutions and high-reliability maintenance - described as the core strengths of the Company
- The conveyor belt market in mining is projected to grow to USD 2.44 billion by 2031 as the industry shifts toward continuous, lower-emission material transport; Asia Pacific leads adoption and India is emerging as a fast-growing market
- India's push for domestic mining, value addition and reduced raw-export reliance is accelerating mineral-processing capacity growth; India's industrial expansion, automation adoption and infrastructure policy support create opportunity across material handling, splicing and engineered service offerings
- Accelerated shift to automated warehouses, IPCC-driven mining operations and digitally enabled asset-management systems expands long-term demand for technologically advanced, service-centric solutions
- Industrial services market growth driven by IoT-enabled monitoring, predictive maintenance and remote diagnostics, aging assets and stricter regulation, supporting outsourced, digitally enabled service models
- Tightening environmental norms globally push customers toward energy-efficient, safer and more sustainable handling systems, giving scope to scale high-value differentiated offerings
- Growing presence in Australia, the Middle East and Latin America improves access to attractive mining markets and positions the Company for larger service contracts and recurring aftermarket opportunities
- FY26 volume/mix commentary: production of moulded and extruded products was 2,799 tonnes, a growth of 11% over the previous year (2,533 tonnes), while adhesives production was 484 tonnes, a dip of about 14% (562 tonnes); exports registered growth of about 21%
- Standalone turnover growth came from both the Manufacturing Division and the Services Division; at the consolidated level profitability was impacted by the Middle East geopolitical situation and the loss at the Saudi Arabian subsidiary, itself driven by reduced income and higher manpower and workshop investment
- Subsidiary-market macro backdrop cited by management: Chile growth easing to about 2.4% in 2026 with copper leadership and lithium expansion; UAE growth projected at 5.6% in 2026 though geopolitics has dragged near-term momentum; Saudi Arabia about 3.1% in 2026 revised up to 4.5% in 2027; Australia in a managed soft landing with mining investment easing as the industry shifts to stable production; Brazil moderate until monetary conditions ease
- Outlook framed as 'cautiously optimistic' - favourable India fundamentals and rising global mining activity, moderated by commodity cycles, regulatory developments, project execution delays, geopolitical uncertainty, currency fluctuations and global macro pressure

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Focus on value-added products in the Manufacturing Division and on profitable site-level operations in the Services and Operation & Maintenance Division
- Complete the approved second phase of expansion of the manufacturing facilities (estimated capex about Rs 40 crore) during FY 2026-27
- Medium-term focus on advanced materials, digital tools and lifecycle-based service models, intended to enhance competitiveness and expand recurring revenue streams
- Build capability in predictive maintenance, remote monitoring and digital optimisation, with management noting customer adoption may be gradual
- Stepped-up Information Technology spending focussed on enhanced digitization and digitalization, with a corresponding increase in professional and computer maintenance costs
- R&D-led product development at the in-house Chennai centre - new products, continuous improvement of existing products, patent filings, and collaborative basic research with academic universities and government agencies
- Strengthen commercial and operational efficiency by onboarding additional talent across key functions; performance-linked increments, incentives and stock options to retain the employee base
- Grow the international subsidiary platform - Saudi Arabia to leverage the manpower and workshop investments made during the year, UAE (TE Global) to build its customer base under strict cost controls, Chile to capitalise on mining/lithium opportunity - with subsidiaries focussed on long-term growth through sustainable business practices
- Agile cost management, technology upgradation and disciplined operational execution as the stated response to competitive and macro pressure
- The Company has formulated a Dividend Distribution Policy in compliance with Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations, published on its website; the policy document itself is not reproduced in this bundle, only the cross-reference. For FY26 the Board recommended, and the AGM notice proposes for declaration, a dividend at the same rate as the previous year, payable out of the profits of the year to members on the record date - so the payout stance is one of continuity rather than a stated payout-ratio formula. Employee participation in value creation is channelled through the Thejo Employees Stock Option Scheme 2015, administered by the Compensation / Nomination and Remuneration Committee and unchanged in substance during the year, with small allotments made through FY26. CSR is treated as a board-governed spend: the CSR Committee formulates the policy and annual action plan and recommends the amount, and the Company confirms it fully met the statutory 2%-of-average-net-profits requirement for the year. Governance oversight of these choices sits with a Board of eleven directors whose Audit Committee and Compensation / Nomination and Remuneration Committee consist wholly of Independent Directors.
- BRSR Section B item 5 records 'N' against all nine NGRBC principles for 'Specific commitments, goals and targets set by the entity with defined timelines' - the Company states it has set NO time-bound ESG targets, and item 6 (performance against such targets) is 'NA' throughout. The ESG content below is therefore programmes and mitigations, not targets.
- Water: the Company operates an STP plant to maintain zero liquid discharge and recycles treated water for gardening; efforts are stated to be underway to optimise water consumption across manufacturing units and to explore rainwater harvesting
- Climate/energy: steps toward energy efficiency and renewable energy adoption including a solar plant at its main manufacturing unit, with agricultural waste fuel used for steam boilers as a lower-emission alternative to fossil fuels
- Circularity: rubber reclaim initiatives and in-house R&D on biodegradation of finished rubber waste, framed as lifecycle stewardship for a long-life product
- Safety: focus on implementing a structured OHS management system covering risk assessments, regular safety training, PPE usage, permit-to-work systems and safety audits across manufacturing and site operations
- ESG governance: policies cover all nine NGRBC principles and have been translated into procedures, but only the Principle 1 policy has been approved by the Board and none of the policies extend to value-chain partners
- ESG governance: the highest authority responsible for implementing and overseeing the Business Responsibility policies is the Managing Director; the Company answers 'No' to having a specified Board Committee or Director responsible for decision-making on sustainability issues, and 'N' across all nine principles to independent external assessment of its policies
- Certification: 'ISO' is the only code/certification/standard named in BRSR Section B item 4, mapped to Principle 2 and Principle 9 (the specific ISO standard numbers are not stated)
- Compliance with statutory requirements relevant to the nine principles is reviewed quarterly based on certification by the MD/WTD, while review of performance against the policies themselves is answered 'N' for all nine principles

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company states it has been focussing on expansion activities and has approved the second phase of expansion of its manufacturing facilities at an estimated capex of about Rs 40 crore, to be completed during FY 2026-27. Its physical footprint as at 31st March 2026 is three plants in India and no international plants, alongside an in-house R&D Centre; the MD&A places the manufacturing facilities and R&D Centre in Chennai and notes distributor networks in various geographies. Overseas, the Board's Report attributes part of the consolidated profitability decline to increased investment in manpower and workshop facilities at the Saudi Arabian subsidiary during the year. On the sustainability side, BRSR Principle 2 records the percentage of R&D and capital expenditure invested in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts as 'Nil', while sustainable-sourcing procedures are stated to be in place with natural rubber comprising about 16% of raw material used at the manufacturing units and an ongoing effort to substitute synthetic rubbers with natural rubber in formulations (the sourcing paragraph is cut off mid-word in this bundle).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated model: 'one of the few companies in the sub-continent offering manufacturing, marketing, and servicing activities under one roof' (MD&A Profile)
- Recurring service revenue base - Maintenance and Repair Services alone account for 45% of sales, with a 74-location national footprint including 37 technical-service and 14 O&M site offices embedded at customer sites
- In-house R&D Centre in Chennai; as at year-end the Company had applied for 48 product patents and three design protections, of which 28 product patents and the three design protections have been awarded
- Global delivery footprint: five overseas subsidiaries (Australia, Saudi Arabia, Brazil, Chile, Ras Al-Khaimah UAE) plus distributor networks, giving access to Australasia, Middle East, South America, North America, Sub-Sahara and West Africa
- Long operating history and listing track record - incorporated 1986, listed on NSE SME-EMERGE in 2012 and migrated to the NSE Main Board in 2023
- Excellence Centre used to train technicians on safety and technical aspects of the job, supporting the services business where 'safety, quality and speed are key'

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Dependence on the mining and commodity capex cycle, with the business concentrated on bulk material handling and mineral processing — The Company states its products and services predominantly cater to Bulk Material Handling and Mineral Processing activities and that 'the business prospects of the Company are closely tied to these activities/industries'. It describes its markets as sensitive to global macroeconomic and commodity-cycle risks, so a downturn in mining investment transmits directly to both the products and the services book.
- Geopolitical disruption - the 2026 Middle East conflict — Management says heightened geopolitical tensions have increased volatility in energy prices, shipping routes and financial markets, potentially affecting mining investment cycles and cost structures. It is already visible in results: consolidated profitability was impacted despite higher revenue, primarily on account of the ongoing geopolitical situation in the Middle East and the loss at the Saudi Arabian subsidiary. Notably, the Risks and Concerns section states the Company 'does not perceive any major technological, operational, financial or environmental risks in the near future except for geopolitical tensions and their impact on the global economy' - geopolitics is the one risk management concedes as live.
- Overseas subsidiary exposure - currency, labour, regulation and country risk — Subsidiaries in Australia, Brazil and Chile are stated to be exposed to fluctuating commodity prices, labour-market rigidities, regulatory changes and currency volatility which may impact profitability. The outlook section repeats that Australia, the Middle East and Latin America carry geopolitical uncertainty, currency fluctuation and differing regulatory environments that could impact profitability and contract execution.
- Competitive intensity and pricing pressure — The industry is described as witnessing intensifying competition from international OEMs, low-cost regional players and integrated automation providers, increasing pricing pressure and shortening product-life cycles.
- Technology transition risk - continuous investment required, customer adoption may lag — As mining and industrial clients accelerate digital adoption, the Company must continuously invest in new technologies, skilled manpower and advanced diagnostics to remain competitive. Management adds that while it is strengthening predictive-maintenance, remote-monitoring and digital-optimisation capability, customer adoption rates may be gradual, requiring sustained investment and posing risks related to technology integration and return on investment.
- Occupational health and safety at customer sites — Flagged as a Risk in the BRSR material-issues table with negative financial implication: on-site servicing at mining, bulk-handling and industrial sites involves exposure to fire, chemical, machinery and fall hazards, and any safety failure can result in worker injury, regulatory action and reputational damage. Mitigation is a structured OHS management system covering risk assessments, safety training, PPE, permit-to-work and safety audits.
- Product quality, reliability and lifecycle stewardship — BRSR material issue flagged as both Risk and Opportunity: conveyor belt failure at customer sites can cause unplanned downtime and safety incidents, and the long product lifecycle creates a stewardship responsibility. Mitigation cited is ISO certification, customer-complaint tracking, rubber reclaim initiatives and in-house R&D on biodegradation of finished rubber waste.
- Environmental compliance and resource dependence - water and GHG emissions — Two BRSR material issues with negative financial implications: manufacturing depends on groundwater, raising consumption and scarcity exposure in the regions where Thejo operates; and energy-intensive rubber and polyurethane processing generates significant GHG emissions with growing customer decarbonisation expectations adding transition risk. The MD&A adds that environmental norms on emissions, water usage and workplace safety are tightening in key markets, potentially increasing compliance and operating costs.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Focus on value-added products in the Manufacturing Division and on profitable site-level operations in the Services and Operation & Maintenance Division
- Complete the approved second phase of expansion of the manufacturing facilities (estimated capex about Rs 40 crore) during FY 2026-27
- Medium-term focus on advanced materials, digital tools and lifecycle-based service models, intended to enhance competitiveness and expand recurring revenue streams
- Build capability in predictive maintenance, remote monitoring and digital optimisation, with management noting customer adoption may be …
